title: Toasted Coconut Cream Pie
summary: Coconut milk custard studded with toasted coconut, chilled in a golden pastry shell and piled high with whipped cream and crisp coconut flakes.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
desiccated or flaked coconut, for toasting

steps.title: Pastry dough
steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt until mostly crumbly with some flat flakes left. Stir in just enough cold water to bring the dough together. Wrap and chill for an hour.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: Roll and line the dish, crimp the edge and chill the case for 30 minutes. Bake at 190 °C (170 °C fan) with paper and beans for 20 minutes, then uncovered for another 10-12 minutes until golden brown. Leave it to cool.

steps.title: Toast the coconut
steps.text: Toast all the coconut (45 g for the custard and 20 g for the top) in the dry frying pan over a medium-low heat, stirring, for 3-5 minutes until patchy gold. Toasting deepens the flavour, but it catches quickly, so keep it moving. Tip out and keep the two amounts separate.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Heat the coconut milk, milk and half the sugar in the saucepan until steaming. Whisk the yolks, remaining sugar, cornflour and salt in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the hot milk. Return everything to the pan and whisk over a medium heat until it boils and turns thick, then cook 1 minute more. Off the heat, stir in the butter, vanilla and the 45 g toasted coconut.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Scrape the warm custard into the cooled case and press cling film onto the surface so no skin forms. Chill for at least 4 hours.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Beat the cream with the 20 g sugar and the vanilla to soft peaks. Pile it on the pie and scatter with the reserved toasted coconut just before serving so it stays crisp.

tips: Shake the tin of coconut milk well before opening so the cream and liquid are evenly mixed.
Do not let the coconut get darker than light gold in the pan; it turns bitter within seconds once it browns.
A frequent mistake is scattering the coconut topping hours ahead, which leaves it soft and chewy.
Desiccated or flaked coconut both work; flaked gives a bolder look on top.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in the fridge, loosely covered, for up to 2 days. Store any extra toasted coconut in an airtight jar at room temperature.
